observation_summary: The compiler fails with a RuntimeException when processing --define flags containing double-quoted strings, and fails to remove certain constant expressions (CALL and NEW nodes) that do not have side effects.
hypothesis: The root cause is twofold: 1) The input validation logic for --define flags in AbstractCommandLineRunner only checked for single-quoted strings, failing to recognize double-quoted strings as valid. 2) The RemoveConstantExpressions pass incorrectly identified CALL and NEW nodes as having side effects, preventing their removal.
prediction: The code will be updated to include a check for double quotes in the --define parsing logic and to explicitly include Token.NEW and Token.CALL in the side-effect check logic.
experiment_rationale: The provided diff shows an added condition in the if-statement for parsing define values (checking for double quotes) and an added condition in the side-effect check for expression nodes (checking for NEW and CALL types). These are classic validation/predicate logic corrections.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves adding missing conditional logic (guards) to validate input formats and to correctly identify node types that do not have side effects. This falls squarely under 'Checking' as it corrects the predicate logic used to validate data and determine control flow.
evidence_used: RemoveConstantExpressions diff adding Token.NEW and Token.CALL checks
